Growing British dividend payers that aim to increase both profits and payouts offer a different way to seek income. This article highlights three stocks from our 2 to 5% yield shortlist that fit that profile. 
 The three stocks below are just a sample from this income theme, and the full screen surfaced 7 more companies with equally detailed stories that are not covered here. To identify, compare, and analyze the highest conviction Type 2 dividend ideas directly, head into the Growing Dividend Payers with 2-5% yield screener . 
 Spirax Group (LSE:SPX) 
 Spirax Group taps directly into the growing dividend payers theme through its Steam Thermal Solutions arm, where industrial steam systems and aftermarket services create recurring cash flows that can support a rising payout without relying on very high headline yields. 
 Spirax Group is a £5.4b thermal energy and fluid technology specialist. It generates around £859 million of revenue from Steam Thermal Solutions, £462 million from Electric Thermal Solutions and £424 million from Watson Marlow, with a business model built around industrial heating, control and pumping systems for essential sectors worldwide. 
 "Spirax Group is strongly positioned to benefit from accelerating customer demand for decarbonization and energy optimization solutions, with a £7b annual addressable market just beginning to open up, and recent Powering Zero orders alongside cross thermal energy assessments now adding early evidence that this pipeline can translate into multi year revenue growth and a richer mix of higher margin electrification projects." 
 What really matters from here is how one quietly building pressure in the background ultimately shapes cash conversion and dividend cover. 
 That pressure on cash conversion is exactly what the full narrative for Spirax Group unpacks, separating short term noise from the longer term dividend ambition and decarbonization opportunity. 
 LSE:SPX Earnings & Revenue History as at Nov 2026 Games Workshop Group (LSE:GAW) 
 Games Workshop Group designs, manufactures, and sells Warhammer tabletop miniatures and games that generate recurring spending on new models, rules, and hobby supplies. The company produced £626.8 million from its Core segment and £32.9 million from Licensing, and has a £5.3b market cap supporting a growing dividend profile. 
 Games Workshop Group fits the 2 to 5% dividend growth theme because its Warhammer ecosystem produces recurring cash flow, supports a 3.02% yield, and has lifted total dividends to £3.00 for 2026/27. Investors focused on rising payouts may watch how shifts in demand across this hobby cycle influence earnings power. 
 Story Continues Those hobby cycle swings matter, so tap into the analysis report for Games Workshop Group to see whether Games Workshop Group's cash generation is keeping pace with its payout ambitions. 
 LSE:GAW Earnings & Revenue History as at Nov 2026 RELX (LSE:REL) 
 RELX brings the growing dividend payer theme into the digital era, with subscription analytics in legal, science and risk quietly doing the heavy lifting behind its income profile. 
 RELX is a £52.5b information and analytics group that earns about £3.5b from Risk, £2.8b from Scientific, Technical & Medical, £1.9b from Legal and £1.2b from Exhibitions, giving dividend investors a mix of recurring data subscriptions and event-led revenue. 
 "RELX's continued rollout and integration of advanced AI-powered analytics and decision tools across its Risk, STM and Legal segments is deepening customer value and increasing product adoption. The expanding use of AI-enabled fraud and identity solutions in Risk, where RELX processes around 145 billion digital transactions each year and over 90% of divisional revenue is already machine-to-machine, creates scope for customers to add more high value tools over time." 
 The real test for RELX is how one unresolved competitive pressure ultimately shows up in pricing power and dividend headroom. 
 That pricing pressure is exactly why the full narrative for RELX digs into where RELX's AI engine is accelerating, where it may be stalling, and how that balance shapes dividend headroom.
